comparison: Both evaluate the core survival and colonization findings (C23, C24, C28-C31) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval includes additional claims about RNAi specificity controls and mechanistic exclusion experiments (C32-C38), while peer review splits these into separate evaluations. Both accept the reduced survival despite reduced colonization phenotype as convincing.

OpenEval R1 includes mechanistic control experiments (C32-C38) that peer review evaluates separately as R2. Both find these SUPPORTED, accepting that pharyngeal pumping and defecation motor program controls rule out trivial behavioral explanations for the phenotype.

Perfect claim overlap (C41-C48) on ER-UPR pathway independence. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval and peer review both accept the XBP-1 overexpression experiment and systematic testing across ER-UPR mutants as demonstrating pathway independence.

Perfect claim overlap (C49-C54) on immunity pathway testing. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED while peer review marks UNCERTAIN. Peer reviewer expressed confusion about differential effects in sek-1 vs pmk-1 mutants, questioning the pathway relationships despite accepting the data.

High overlap (C56-C61, C64) on context-dependent immune effects in immunocompromised backgrounds. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval includes additional claims (C55, C63) about convergence of survival rates. Both accept this as a key novel finding showing beneficial effects in immunodeficiency contexts.

Perfect claim overlap (C65-C77) on RNA-seq and intracellular pathogen response signature. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED while peer review marks UNCERTAIN. Peer reviewers questioned why intracellular pathogen genes rather than PMK-1 targets were enriched, and noted the intracellular pathogen mimicry argument was not thoroughly investigated.

OpenEval R6 addresses functional validation of transcriptomic findings (C78-C81) while peer R7 covers both these claims and ELT-2 experiments (C82-C90). OpenEval finds R6 SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about partial rescue. Peer review marks R7 UNCERTAIN due to concerns about double RNAi methodology and lack of sufficiency experiments.

High overlap (C82-C90) on ELT-2 as key mediator. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate acknowledgment of incomplete rescue. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about double RNAi experiments lacking proper controls and requesting loss-of-function mutant validation and sufficiency experiments.

High overlap (C5-C8, C91-C96, C101) on main conclusions about aberrant immune response. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as synthesis of experimental evidence. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, challenging novelty claims and questioning whether effects result from immune activation versus compromised general health/physiology.

OpenEval R8 includes C9 among main conclusions found SUPPORTED. Peer R9 evaluates C9 separately as UNCERTAIN, tied to concerns about incomplete validation of ELT-2 mechanistic experiments and the use of double RNAi without proper controls.

OpenEval R9 evaluates background knowledge and prior work claims (C1-C4, C10-C22, C25-C27, C35, C39-C40, C62, C73, C75, C83, C97-C100, C102-C104, C106-C109) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on experimental claims rather than background literature.

OpenEval R10 evaluates C105 (speculative mechanisms) as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of experimental evidence to distinguish between proposed mechanisms. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific speculative claim.
